transcript.text: We had a power cut last night and now our Candy washer dryer is completely dead - no lights, nothing. Everything else in the house came back on. The plug fuse is fine, I swapped it. Help!

A sound plug fuse does not prove the washer-dryer is receiving power. After a power cut, the first thing to rule out is the exact socket or any separate switched/fused spur feeding it. 1. Switch the washer-dryer off and unplug it.
2. Plug a known-working low-power item, such as a lamp or phone charger, into the same wall socket.
3. Check for a nearby switched spur/fused connection unit and make sure it is switched on.
4. While unplugged, make sure the washer-dryer plug is fully seated when refitted and inspect the lead for obvious cuts, crushing or scorching. If that socket has no power, it is a house supply/socket issue. These need an appliance engineer, as diagnosis involves internal mains wiring. If there was a pop, bang, burning smell or any scorching around the plug or machine, leave it unplugged and arrange an engineer rather than trying it again.
I've already tried a lamp in that socket and it works fine. No bang or burning smell, lead and plug look fine too. Tried unplugging for 10+ minutes as well, still totally dead. What next?

The supply to the socket is proven, so this is now most likely an internal incoming-power fault rather than anything you can reset. A power cut/surge can damage the mains interference suppressor (mains filter), which is the first electrical component inside the machine; the other main possibilities are an incoming connector/wiring fault or the power-supply section of the control PCB. There is no further useful owner-safe check for a completely dead washer-dryer. Leave it unplugged and arrange an appliance engineer/electrician experienced in white goods. Ask them to trace the incoming power path—mains filter, wiring/connectors and any power switch—before condemning the control PCB. The PCB should be the last conclusion, not the first. As there has been no bang, burning smell or visible lead damage, this does not necessarily mean the machine is unsafe to have in the kitchen, but do not keep plugging it in or attempt internal inspection/repair yourself.
